Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — InfiniteMed is excited about the latency profile and cost numbers. Before we progress to procurement I need to validate a couple of residency items for our DPO and legal team: 

1) Can Redwood delegate per-customer region pinning at the account level (EU-only) while still allowing short-lived cross-region processing for operational reasons (e.g., cache warm-up, model hot-shard sync)? If so, what are the guardrails and maximum window you allow?

2) We need a list of subprocessors that will have transient access during those windows (edge caches, telemetry, analytics). Ideally that list is a roster with activation dates and minimal access scopes.

3) For audit we need an acceptance criterion: evidence you can supply if we request a one-off proof that no token-level data left the EU for a specific day/time range. What format do you deliver — operator logs, KMS audit events, or an affidavit?

Can you loop in legal/ops and share a proposed DPA addendum or annex that captures (1)-(3)? We have a launch target in Q1 and need to close this before contract signature.

Best,
Diane
Diane Park
CISO, InfiniteMed Health

Hi Diane — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Ben (ops) to draft a concise annex. Quick answers up front to keep momentum:

• Region pinning: Yes — customers can request EU-only placement by default. We support account-level pinning plus per-route overrides.
• Temporary cross-region windows: We allow short-lived operational windows (default = 72 hours, configurable up to 7 days with approval). All such windows are logged and require explicit escalation in our control plane.
• Subprocessors: We maintain an activation roster; during transient windows only a reduced set (edge CDN, telemetry-forwarder, ops-metering) have elevated reach.
• Evidence: We can provide time-bound attestations using combined operator logs + KMS event correlation; for higher-assurance customers we can provide an export of anonymized telemetry plus cryptographic audit trail.

Marissa / Ben — can you draft a DPA addendum that:
  1) Specifies the max transient window and scope (default 72h).
  2) Includes a signed subprocessor activation roster & notification cadence.
  3) Describes the evidence package (logs + KMS events) and expected SLA for producing it (5 business days by default).

Diane — I uploaded the initial template to our Drive and attached a sketched ops map. Please let us know any non-starters.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Diane — thanks for the questions. Drafting notes below and a short-attestation workflow we propose. I attached a draft addendum (Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.pdf) with tracked sections for comments. Key points: 

1) Definitions: 
   - "Pinning" = account-level region preference where production inference and persistent storage remain within EU data centers.
   - "Transient window" = a controlled operational period where ephemeral processing may cross borders for cache warm-up, model shard sync, or disaster-recovery, bounded by explicit activation.

2) Default limits and approvals: 
   - Default transient window = 72 hours unless InfiniteMed requests a longer window in writing. 
   - Any window >72 hours requires approvals from Redwood security and an exec sponsor at InfiniteMed.

3) Subprocessor roster & activation model: 
   - Roster will enumerate each subprocessor, purpose, access scope, and whether activation is automatic or on-demand.
   - For transient windows only: activation scope reduced to session-level KV access and no long-term storage writes.

4) Evidence package (requested by you): 
   - We will deliver operator log slices (UTC timestamps), KMS event identifiers mapping to the same time-window, and a signed statement from our security lead.
   - Standard delivery SLA = 5 business days; expedited (48 hours) possible for critical requests (fees may apply).

5) Auditability & privacy constraints: 
   - To protect other customers, logs are delivered as scoped exports with redaction of unrelated tenant identifiers.

Next steps: Ben can provide the operational map and a short example CSV of a subprocessor activation record. Diane — if this aligns I will mark the addendum as draft and we can run it through your procurement team.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Diane — quick ops note and sample CSV attached (pinning-ops-map.png was the visual; sample roster in Drive).

Operational constraints we implement when a transient window is opened: 
- Traffic is routed back to EU primary while bursts are served from regional edge caches; edge caches only hold encrypted KV caches and are configured with TTLs not to persist for more than the window.
- All activations require a signed control-plane API call (audit trail) plus a support ticket number.
- KMS keys for data at rest will remain in EU; any crypto operations that must occur outside the region use wrapped keys and emit KMS events we can map back.

Example activation CSV header: timestamp_utc,subprocessor,activation_type,scope,operator_ticket
2027-11-22T02:12:00Z,EdgeCacheInc,auto,session_kv,SUP-1243

I put the sample CSV and a redacted activation example in the shared Drive folder. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min ops walkthrough with our SREs to show the control-plane UI and run a simulated activation.

Ben Carter
